en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle is the largest and one of the rarest eagles in the world, primarily found in the forests of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley region.
Lake Mainit in Mindanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a maximum depth of about 223 meters.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippine Sea contains the Philippine Trench, which drops to a depth of over 10,000 meters east of the archipelago.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes for night hunting.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making it a rare navigable underground river.
The San Juanico Bridge connects the islands of Leyte and Samar, spanning the narrow San Juanico Strait.
Marinduque is a heart-shaped island province in the Mimaropa region, geographically located south of the island of Luzon.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
